title: Rate Lock Commitment Appraisal-Delay Waiver: Covered Days and Waived Amount
content:
When Larkspur waives a **Rate Lock Commitment** extension charge for an appraisal delay, the amount follows from the extension named and the appraisal dates.

The extension concerned is the lock's borrower-borne extension entry with the highest extension number. Its extension days, Larkspur-borne days, cost points and cost amount are read from that entry.

1. **Appraisal-delay days.** The appraisal-delay days are the calendar days by which the file's appraisal report was completed after its due date. Both dates are read from the **Appraisal Order**.
2. **Covered days.** The covered days of the extension are the appraisal-delay days, never more than the lock's lender-delay allowance, less the lender-delay days already relieved on the lock before this waiver. Those relieved days are the Larkspur-borne days booked on its extensions beyond the complimentary days, plus, for the lock's waiver entries, their waived dollars divided by the dollar value of one day at the lock's standard per-day cost. That dollar value is the loan amount at lock times the product's extension cost per day in basis points, divided by 10,000. The covered days are never below zero, are counted in whole days with any fraction of a day dropped, and are never more than the extension's charged days, which are its extension days less its Larkspur-borne days. This measure of covered days applies to a waiver Larkspur books on its own initiative, and only to such a waiver; an extension booking measures its appraisal-delay days under the extension-charge rules.
3. **Waived amount.** The waived amount is the covered days times the extension's per-day points (its cost points divided by its charged days), rounded to three decimal places, times the loan amount at lock divided by 100, rounded to the cent.

The lender-delay allowance and the complimentary days are those of the lock's product.

### Worked example (hypothetical inputs, on a Larkspur 45-Day Rate Lock)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Extension entry | Extension number 1: 10 days, 0 Larkspur-borne, cost points 0.200 |
| Charged days | 10 |
| Per-day points | 0.200 divided by 10, which is 0.020 |
| Appraisal completed after its due date | 6 days |
| Allowance | 15 days; nothing relieved before |
| Covered days | 6 (not more than 10) |
| Waived points | 6 times 0.020, which is 0.120 |
| Loan amount at lock | $400,000.00 |
| Waived amount | $480.00 |

*Hypothetical second case:* the lock has an earlier waiver entry of $160.00 at a loan amount at lock of $400,000.00 and 2.0 basis points per day. One day is worth $80.00, so 2 days are already relieved. With the same 6-day appraisal delay, the covered days are 6 less 2, which is 4. Had $100.00 been waived, 1.25 days would be relieved, and 6 less 1.25, which is 4.75, counts as 4 whole days.
